# Prospects {#prospects-section}

## What we want to discover {#next-questions}

![](media/prospects/discovery-map.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 600px;" fig-alt="Open questions placed on a neutrino-energy axis from 1 TeV to 1 EeV over the measured cosmic neutrino spectrum: Seyfert galaxies beyond NGC 1068 at 1.5 to 15 TeV; the spectral break near 25 TeV, pp or p-gamma; the Milky Way and PeVatrons above 200 TeV; the neutrino cross section from Earth absorption above 40 TeV; the Glashow resonance at 6.3 PeV; and KM3-230213A at about 220 PeV, source or cosmogenic. Transients through alerts and new physics can appear at any energy."}

::: {.media-caption}
Questions on the energy axis · Spectrum: [IceCube (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22233v3) · [Glashow: IceCube (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051) · [KM3-230213A: KM3NeT (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08543-1)
:::

## What we lack {#what-we-need}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Instruments and analysis

| What is missing | Why it matters |
|:---|:---|
| Northern exposure beyond $10\,\mathrm{km}^3$ | Faint sources and the Galactic Centre seen through the Earth |
| Sharper cascade directions | All flavours point back to sources |
| More events above $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$ | The spectrum's end, Glashow events, the 100 PeV puzzle |
| Global alerts, joint analyses, open data | One sky, several telescopes |
| Calibrated optics of water and ice | Energies and directions we can trust |
| Population theory within the gamma-ray budget | Turning many faint hints into sources |

### People

![](media/prospects/people-chain.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-width: 1450px; --media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Symbolic chain: the programme ФНАФЧ, neutrino physics and particle astrophysics, with courses, seminars and the Baikal school; people, students who become researchers and lecturers; results, data analysis, for example the Milky Way in Baikal-GVD data with a first author from the programme; and the next experiment, B-HUNT, Russia and China."}

## Where are the sources? {#conclusions}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="66%"}
![](media/prospects/sources-sky.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px;" fig-alt="Equatorial sky map. The Galactic plane with the Galactic Centre is marked as diffuse neutrino emission from the Milky Way. NGC 1068 stands for Seyfert galaxies, TXS 0506+056 for blazars, and an open circle marks the direction of KM3-230213A, whose origin is open. Caption: most of the flux comes from many faint sources, not yet resolved."}
:::
::: {.column width="31%"}
**Found:** our Galaxy · NGC 1068 and Seyfert galaxies · blazar candidates.

**Still open:** most of the flux — a crowd of faint sources.

**Next:** bigger telescopes and networks — B-HUNT, KM3NeT, IceCube-Gen2.
:::
:::::

::: {.question}
We have found where to look. Next we must resolve the crowd.
